incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT: streaming_tail_latency.p99 > 5s (eu-west-1). paging @olivia-oncall. auto-triage created: stream-tail-surge-1763400000.

olivia: I'm on call. seeing the alert, pulling dashboards (p95/p99). which routes?

sam: looks concentrated on /v1/stream (sse + ws) served by proxy-gateway-eu-2. p95 jumped from ~180ms -> 1.1s over last 3m; p99 from ~700ms -> 6.5s. num_active_streams up 20%.

marco: logs show a cluster of write stalls to client sockets: repeated `write timeout` followed by `downstream reset`. sample trace: trace_id=tr-7c9a2b. upstreams (model backends) look fine — tokens being produced. problem is delivery to clients.

olivia: ok good to know backend is healthy. can someone run quick grep on proxy queue metrics and consumer backlog?

sam: running queries now. `promql: increase(stream_send_queue_length{region="eu-west-1"}[5m])` -> +14k queued events. also `sum(rate(proxy_write_time_seconds_bucket[1m]))` shows high tail.

marco: fetching proxy logs from gateway node id=gw-eu-2-7:``` 
[2026-03-15T12:00:05Z] stream.write timeout after 10s (conn_id=abc123)
[2026-03-15T12:00:06Z] conn abc123 send_queue=124, client_rtt=200ms
[2026-03-15T12:00:07Z] conn abc124 write error: EPIPE
```

karen: likely client backpressure: a subset of clients can't accept chunks fast enough, causing the gateway send queues to fill and head-of-line blocking for other connections. we saw similar pattern when regional load balancer slowed TLS handshakes last quarter.

olivia: immediate mitigation options?

karen: two quick levers:
1) enable per-connection send-queue caps and drop excessively stalled streams (graceful close) via feature flag `edge.stream_backpressure_strict=true` (rollout small first).
2) temporarily shift traffic from gateway `proxy-gateway-eu-2` to `proxy-gateway-eu-1` (same region, different pool) using routing weight change.

marco: i can flip traffic. scaling proxies will take ~30s to spawn new pods; drop/close is near-instant. i'm in favor of dropping a small % of stuck streams to recover tail.

sam: consequences? customers on affected streams will see early termination. we should target only streams with queue > 300 or stalled > 8s. runbook suggests 10% threshold. ops-runbook-bot, share link?

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: Streaming tail/stall (internal) -> https://redwood.infra/runbooks/stream-tail-stall. Recommended steps: (A) apply temporary queue cap, (B) adjust routing weights, (C) monitor p99 and error counts. Page severity guidance included.

olivia: OK, Marco - proceed with selective closes AND route shift. Sam - prepare dashboard/watch alerts to watch p95/p99, error_rate, and dropped_streams metric. I'll post comms for potential customer impact.

marco: executing selective close script:``` 
# close streams with queue > 300 and stalled > 8s
kubectl exec -n infra proxy-gateway-eu-2-7 -- /bin/proxyctl close-stalled --queue-threshold=300 --stalled-seconds=8 --dry-run=false
```

marco: applied. rolling small traffic weight 20% -> 0 for proxy-gateway-eu-2, routing weight to proxy-gateway-eu-1.``` 
kubectl patch cm routing-config -n infra -p '{"data":{"gw-eu-2-weight":"0","gw-eu-1-weight":"100"}}'```

sam: watching metrics: p99 decreased from 6.5s -> 1.8s within 45s; p95 back to ~220ms. queued events dropping. dropped_streams metric incremented by ~3.2%.

olivia: nice — looks like mitigation worked. any customer-facing incidents? which customers hit the dropped_streams?

sam: correlating tenant IDs from logs. affected tenants: tenant-omega, tenant-beta (low-volume), and a small set of mobile clients with flaky network. total impacted streams ~1.9% of active streams in region.

karen: recommend targeted email for tenants with >5 dropped streams, internal CS ping for higher-touch accounts. set status page?

olivia: agree. I'll create a brief status update: "Degraded streaming delivery for eu-west-1 between 12:00-12:05 UTC, partial stream terminations for small subset; mitigation applied and p99 recovered." Sam, please paste affected tenant list (sanitized) to #support.

sam: pasted to #support (PM/CS) with tenant IDs and timestamps.

marco: follow-up actions: enable `edge.stream_backpressure_strict=true` on eu-1 and eu-2 as a controlled rollout (5% -> 25%). Also add prom alert to fire when send_queue increase > 5k in 5m. I'll open a PR to add queue cap config to proxy helm chart.

olivia: assigning follow-ups: Marco (config PR + traffic routing playbook), Sam (customer impact notes + metrics alert), Karen (post-incident doc + CS comm template). I'm going to hand over to Aya for follow-up and postmortem since my shift ends in 40m. Aya, you available?

aya: I'm here, taking over oncall. I'll keep watch for 30m and start the postmortem doc. please add any logs/traces to the ticket.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-1763400000. Link: https://redwood.infra/incidents/INC-1763400000. Attachments: metrics snapshot, sample traces.

olivia: thanks team. summary for postmortem: root cause likely client backpressure + proxy send-queue without strict caps -> head-of-line blocking -> tail p99 spike. mitigation: selective close + route traffic + apply strict caps. customer impact: ~1.9% streams in region briefly terminated, <0.5% high-touch tenants, no data loss (clients can reconnect). next steps: PR for helm config, alert tuning, runbook update.

aya: taking notes and will own the postmortem. leaving thread open for any late artifacts. I'll update INC ticket within 4 hours. :white_check_mark:

olivia: handing to aya. signing off from active oncall here. :wave:

sam: one small note — we should investigate LB TLS handshake latencies from 11:30->12:00 window; there were spikes concurrent with stream queue growth. adding to postmortem list.

marco: ack. I'll bundle TLS LB traces with the proxy logs in the incident ticket.

aya: thanks — will coordinate. closing operational loop: p99 stabilized <1s for last 3m. monitoring for 15m before marking resolved.

incident-bot: Monitoring note: p99 < 1s sustained for 5m. incident state: mitigation in place.
